declaredScopeIssues: Graduate systems biology and computational neuroscience currently share biology/systems-biology. Its earliest reaction-network and flux-balance tasks unnecessarily require the complete biology/neuroscience and animal-physiology ancestry; these working capabilities need a separate accessible quantitative-cellular destination connected to the neural continuation.

Graduate stochastic-process theory in mathematics/stochastic-processes currently requires numerical methods and differential equations for every learner, although its first measure-theoretic probability and Markov-chain tasks do not need that preparation. A separate probability/process foundation and connected stochastic-calculus continuation are needed.

Undergraduate computational physics in physics/computational-physics imposes optimization and statistical inference on first forward-simulation tasks. The forward simulation and field-solver route should be separated from the inverse-modeling continuation.

chemistry/advanced-inorganic-chemistry promises kinetic discrimination of catalytic mechanisms but does not require chemistry/kinetics or locally teach rate-law derivation and fitting. Its graduate catalytic-inference preparation remains insufficient.

The current inventory does not yet provide independently assessable graduate algebraic geometry or analytic/algebraic number-theory foundations beyond elementary number theory and graduate algebra; these established mathematical continuations remain unfinished.

Established working and graduate foundations for computer vision, robotics/control and information theory are not independently specified. Graphics, classical AI, optimization and signal analysis do not by themselves teach their distinctive inverse-inference, state-estimation and coding methods.
The coverage inventory lacks matching deferred rows for the unfinished mathematical and computing domains identified above; those domains must not be treated as available preparation.
interpretation: Structural validity and traceability do not establish completeness or learner readiness. Higher-level sources, alternate paths, and other source outcomes are inspection signals, not automatic defects. Do not delete edges or split decks without evaluating their contracts.

exclusions.subject: mathematics
exclusions.rationale: Arithmetic geometry, higher categories and specialized set-theoretic independence programs are beyond this representative progression; algebra, topology and logic have separate included working and graduate contracts.

exclusions.subject: computer-science
exclusions.domain: Vendor qualifications and exhaustive frontier computing
exclusions.rationale: Vendor stacks, certification syllabi and exhaustive frontier architectures are excluded; systems construction, learning, security and verification are taught independently of implementations.

exclusions.subject: chemistry
exclusions.domain: Credentials and exhaustive specialist chemical catalogs
exclusions.rationale: Specialist chemical manufacturing authorization, named instrument certifications and exhaustive reaction catalogs are excluded; durable process, analytical and synthetic methods are included.

exclusions.subject: biology
exclusions.domain: Professional clinical qualifications and exhaustive taxonomy
exclusions.rationale: Clinical, veterinary and regulated practitioner qualifications and exhaustive taxon-specific expertise are separate destinations; biological mechanisms, experimental methods and translational judgment remain included.

exclusions.subject: physics
exclusions.domain: Additional frontier theories and professional engineering qualifications
exclusions.rationale: String theory, exhaustive detector engineering and specialized geophysical or aerospace qualifications are excluded; this progression includes field theory, experimental inference, continuum mechanics and astrophysics.

includes: Operational semantics, interpreters, types, binding and programming paradigms

outcomes.description: Compare functional, object-oriented and declarative abstraction through equivalent programs and modularity tradeoffs.
Define operational rules and implement interpreters with environments, closures, mutation and explicit evaluation strategies.
Construct a simple static type checker and prove bounded progress and preservation claims by structural induction.

practice: Implement two evaluation strategies for a typed language and use proofs and tests to expose their behavioral differences.

includes: Threat modeling, application and systems attacks, cryptographic use, privacy and defense
excludes: Unauthorized exploitation and advanced cryptographic proofs

outcomes.description: Explain modular arithmetic, encryption, authentication, signatures and key exchange; select standard primitives and diagnose protocol misuse.
Implement least privilege, validation and monitoring; justify privacy, disclosure and incident-response decisions with evidence.
Construct threat models and reproduce bounded memory, injection, authentication and network attacks in authorized sandboxes.

practice: Threat-model an isolated application, demonstrate authorized vulnerabilities and verify fixes with regression and abuse-case tests.

includes: Requirements, modular design, testing, version control, delivery and professional tradeoffs

outcomes.description: Use version control, issue tracking, automated builds and release procedures; diagnose regressions and document operational risks.
Design modular interfaces, refactor code and construct unit, integration and property-based tests with reviewable evidence.
Elicit and prioritize requirements, define acceptance criteria and justify privacy, accessibility and stakeholder tradeoffs.

practice: Deliver a team-maintained application change through requirements negotiation, code review, continuous testing and a release retrospective.

includes: Groups, actions, quotient structures, rings, ideals, polynomials and fields

outcomes.description: Construct finite fields and elementary field extensions and determine minimal polynomials and extension degrees.
Prove group and homomorphism properties; calculate actions, quotient groups and finite-group structure using Sylow theorems.
Construct quotient rings and ideals; prove divisibility and factorization results in integers and polynomial rings.

practice: Classify an unfamiliar small algebraic structure and prove its quotient and field-extension properties.

includes: Fundamental groups, coverings, chain complexes, homology and exact-sequence calculations

outcomes.description: Prove bounded invariance, fixed-point and nonretraction consequences and compare spaces through computable invariants.
Construct simplicial and singular chain complexes and compute homology with boundary maps and exact sequences.
Calculate fundamental groups and covering-space relationships using homotopy and van Kampen arguments.

practice: Compute fundamental groups and homology of unfamiliar glued spaces and prove a topological obstruction.

includes: Limits, derivatives, integrals, differential models and series in one variable

outcomes.description: Calculate limits and derivatives and solve related-rate, extremum and local-linearization problems.
Apply the fundamental theorem, substitution, integration by parts and improper integrals to accumulation models.
Analyze sequences and series; construct Taylor approximations and bound truncation errors under stated conditions.

practice: Derive an accumulation model, calculate its optimum and compare exact, graphical and Taylor-based solutions.

includes: Enumerative methods, formal generating functions, graph invariants and extremal arguments

outcomes.description: Solve counting problems with bijections, inclusion-exclusion, recurrences and formal generating functions.
Establish elementary extremal and Ramsey bounds using double counting, induction and pigeonhole arguments.
Prove results about trees, connectivity, matchings, colorings and planar graphs using explicit constructions.

practice: Count constrained objects in two ways and prove a sharp or bounded graph-theoretic claim.

includes: Holomorphic functions, contour integration, residues, conformal maps and harmonic applications

outcomes.description: Analyze complex differentiability, power series and analytic continuation; prove elementary Cauchy-Riemann and holomorphic-function results.
Use conformal maps and analytic functions to evaluate real integrals and solve bounded harmonic-potential problems.
Prove and apply Cauchy integral results, Laurent expansions and residue methods with explicit contour estimates.

practice: Evaluate a parameterized real integral by residues and solve a transformed planar boundary-value problem.

includes: First-order equations, linear higher-order equations, systems, phase portraits and elementary numerical stepping

outcomes.description: Construct phase portraits, linearize equilibria, classify stability and implement hand-calculated Euler steps with error comparisons.
Solve separable and linear first-order equations and constant-coefficient forced second-order initial-value problems.
Solve linear systems using eigenstructure and matrix exponentials; interpret coupled state representations.

practice: Derive a coupled flow model, solve its linear case and compare phase portraits and time-step approximations.

includes: Parametrized curves and surfaces, curvature, fundamental forms and geodesics

outcomes.description: Calculate arc length, curvature, torsion and moving frames of curves in two and three dimensions.

Compute tangent planes, first and second fundamental forms, Gaussian and mean curvature of parametrized surfaces.

practice: Compare intrinsic and extrinsic geometry on unfamiliar surfaces and calculate geodesics in selected coordinate charts.

includes: Arithmetic, algebra, functions, units, elementary geometry, trigonometry and coordinate vectors

outcomes.description: Manipulate fractions, powers, logarithms, equations and inequalities; interpret polynomial, exponential and trigonometric functions.
Calculate lengths, areas, volumes and angles; use similarity, trigonometry and two- or three-dimensional coordinate vectors.
Translate tables, graphs and verbal models into equations; track units, scales, significant figures and estimation errors.

practice: Model an unfamiliar geometric measurement problem, solve it algebraically and check units, scale and graphical consistency.

includes: Banach and Hilbert spaces, duality, bounded operators, weak convergence and spectral theory

outcomes.description: Apply Hahn-Banach, uniform boundedness and open-mapping results; analyze weak convergence and operator adjoints.
Construct Banach, Hilbert and Lp spaces and prove completeness, projection and duality results.
Prove compact self-adjoint spectral results and solve bounded variational and eigenfunction approximation problems.

practice: Establish existence and spectral approximation for an unfamiliar compact-operator or coercive variational problem.

includes: Modules, structure theorems, Galois theory and finite-group representations

outcomes.description: Prove and apply Galois correspondence and determine solvability and constructibility for polynomial examples.
Construct modules, tensor products and exact sequences and apply structure theorems over principal ideal domains.
Construct finite-group representations and character tables and prove decomposition and orthogonality results.

practice: Determine a splitting field and Galois group and decompose a related finite-dimensional group representation.

includes: Distributions, Sobolev spaces, weak formulations, energy methods and Galerkin approximation

outcomes.description: Derive and implement Galerkin and elementary finite-element approximations and establish bounded convergence and error estimates.
Prove bounded elliptic and evolutionary existence, uniqueness and stability results using coercivity, compactness and energy estimates.
Construct distributions and Sobolev spaces and formulate weak derivatives, traces and boundary-value problems.

practice: Prove well-posedness for a weak boundary problem and implement a mesh-refinement study verifying its approximation estimate.

includes: Linear systems, vector spaces, linear maps, eigenproblems and least squares

outcomes.description: Construct bases and coordinate changes; prove elementary claims about vector spaces and linear maps.
Compute eigenstructure, orthogonal projections, least-squares solutions, quadratic forms and singular-value decompositions.
Solve matrix systems by elimination; characterize rank, null spaces, consistency and determinants.

practice: Recover a linear transformation from data and compare exact inversion with least-squares and singular-value solutions.

outcomes.description: Formalize first-order syntax, semantics and derivations and prove soundness and bounded completeness constructions.
Develop arithmetization and representability sufficiently to prove a stated incompleteness theorem and distinguish its assumptions.
Apply compactness and elementary model constructions to distinguish semantic consequence, categoricity and expressibility.

practice: Formalize a theory, construct a compactness application and present a complete bounded incompleteness argument.

includes: Smooth manifolds, tangent bundles, tensors, differential forms, connections and curvature

outcomes.description: Compute metrics, Levi-Civita connections, geodesics and curvature tensors and distinguish intrinsic geometric invariants.

Construct smooth atlases, tangent and cotangent bundles, vector fields and tensor transformations on explicit manifolds.

outcomes.description: Calculate joint, marginal and transformed densities, moments and sampling distributions using multivariable integration.
Derive moment, likelihood and conjugate Bayesian estimators; compare bias, variance, sufficiency and information bounds.

practice: Derive and compare exact, asymptotic and Bayesian intervals for a new parametric sampling model.

practice: Construct convergence counterexamples and prove an unfamiliar parameter-dependent integration result.

Calculate line and surface integrals, divergence and curl; apply Green, Stokes and divergence theorems.
Evaluate multiple integrals in Cartesian, polar, cylindrical and spherical coordinates with correct Jacobians.

practice: Compute mass, flux and a constrained optimum for a three-dimensional model, checking coordinate-independent agreement.

Solve modular systems and establish Fermat, Euler and elementary quadratic-reciprocity consequences.
Solve bounded Diophantine problems using descent, congruences, continued fractions and rational approximation.

practice: Solve an unfamiliar integer equation and prove the completeness or explicit limits of the solution method.

practice: Build a tested numerical library and expose failure cases involving ill-conditioning, unstable steps and misleading residuals.

Derive first- and second-order conditions, KKT systems and elementary dual bounds under stated regularity assumptions.

practice: Solve a constrained allocation and fitting problem, checking optimality certificates and sensitivity to initialization and scaling.

Calculate discrete expectations, variances, joint distributions and binomial or Poisson predictions.

practice: Compare competing probability models for an unfamiliar observation process using exact enumeration and supplied distribution tables.

Prove sequence and series convergence using completeness, Cauchy criteria and rigorous estimates.

practice: Develop proofs and counterexamples for a family of parameterized function sequences and their integral limits.

practice: Prove a stopping or convergence result and compare analytic hitting predictions with a validated stochastic simulation.

Analyze product and quotient spaces and establish homeomorphisms or topological obstructions in concrete examples.
Construct topologies and continuous maps and compare metric, subspace, separation and countability properties.

practice: Classify unfamiliar quotient-space examples and prove or refute compactness and connectedness claims.

practice: Compare approximation methods for an unfamiliar transition or scattering problem and model a reduced-state decoherence experiment.

Analyze normal modes, phase-space stability, separatrices and bounded examples of nonlinear resonance and chaos.
Derive Euler-Lagrange equations, constrained-coordinate models and Noether conservation laws through explicit action variations.

practice: Derive and analyze a constrained coupled mechanical system in both Lagrangian and Hamiltonian representations.

Implement particle and oscillator simulations with conservation-aware integration and convergence comparisons.

Calculate electromagnetic energy, momentum and bounded dipole-radiation patterns using retarded potentials.

practice: Solve a dielectric boundary and antenna problem, checking Maxwell boundary conditions and energy accounting.

practice: Build an instrumented resonance or optical experiment and submit code, calibration records, spectral diagnostics and a model-comparison report.

includes: Continuum stress, conservation, viscous flow, dimensional analysis, waves and compressibility

Use dimensionless groups to analyze stability, surface waves, compressible flow and shock jump conditions.

practice: Derive and test a flow model for unfamiliar geometry, comparing exact profiles, scaling estimates and measured pressure loss.

includes: Lorentzian geometry, Einstein equations, black holes, gravitational waves and relativistic cosmology

Derive Einstein equations from a bounded variational treatment and solve symmetric vacuum and cosmological examples.
Construct Lorentzian metrics, stress-energy tensors, covariant conservation and geodesic observables with explicit coordinate conventions.

practice: Measure a physical constant with two methods and reconcile discrepancies through calibration and an uncertainty budget.

Calculate centers of mass, moments of inertia, torque, angular momentum and simple rigid-body rotation.

practice: Predict and experimentally compare a rolling or orbital motion, checking forces, conservation and limiting cases.

Calculate Lorentz transformations, spacetime intervals and relativistic energy-momentum conservation in one-dimensional events.

practice: Infer hidden energies or lifetimes from unfamiliar spectral and decay observations and solve a relativistic collision.

practice: Design a laser-based imaging or sensing system and validate propagation, resolution and noise predictions with safe data or apparatus.

practice: Compare particle, fluid and kinetic predictions for a plasma-wave dataset and justify the regime and stability assumptions.

practice: Analyze a nonstandard thermal cycle and compare predicted work and entropy production with supplied measurements.

practice: Measure resonances and an optical interference pattern, comparing fitted parameters with independently measured geometry.
